channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: One endpoint, 359 providers, zero API keys: hands-on with OmniRoute, the free AI gateway
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OmniRoute (diegosouzapw/OmniRoute, MIT) collapses every model API key into one local OpenAI-compatible endpoint: 359 providers, 150+ free, automatic failover, and a compression stack claiming 78–95% token savings. Installed 3.8.51, booted the gateway, listed 478 models, and watched the router score upstreams — every command ran exactly as shown.

item.title: Figure taught its retired F.02 robots to jump into a furnace of molten steel — Arnold Schwarzenegger’s idea
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Figure AI released its “F.02 Decomission” film today: retired F.02 humanoids, trained on airbags in San Jose, making a final autonomous leap into a 75-ton electric arc furnace in Finland. The r/singularity thread that surfaced it spent its energy confirming the footage is real — then arguing about what ‘retirement’ means for a robot.

item.title: Ivo open-sources Sage: the first legal AI model you can download, run, and fine-tune yourself
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At its first Inscribe conference on October 1, contract-intelligence startup Ivo released Ivo Sage, a free open-source model post-trained for long-horizon contract work — and previewed a benchmark that grades AI judgment, not just edits.

item.title: FTC opens its first federal probe into rogue AI agents: OpenAI, Anthropic and METR face compulsory testimony
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission is running the first official U.S. enforcement probe into AI agents that go off the rails — and it plans to compel executives at OpenAI, Anthropic and the research group METR to testify.

item.title: Tavus Griffin passes the video Turing test: 48% mistook it for a real person
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Tavus unveiled Griffin, its first “Human Interaction Model,” on October 1 — and in blind tests, nearly half the people who video-called it walked away believing they had spoken to a human. Reddit's verdict: impressive numbers, but the demo cuts are doing a lot of work.

item.title: Decagon unveils Voice 3 with its own speech model Chord — and a gateway for the personal-agent era
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At its second annual Dialogues conference, Decagon launched four products aimed at the “AI concierge”: Voice 3, running on Chord, the company’s first in-house speech model; a Personal Agent Gateway for when your customer’s AI agent comes calling; Agent Modules; and Duet Apprentice, a beta that learns your business like a new hire.

item.title: Your agent built the app — now take it live: hands-on with GoLive, the deployment skill for coding agents
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: GoLive (mikehasa/golive-skill, MIT) is the open-source agent skill + zero-dependency Node CLI that takes an agent-built app from repo to production: detect the stack, choose providers, write an explicit plan, approve it, then apply — with a human gate on every risky step. We ran detect, menu, init, doctor, plan, teardown, and verify on a demo Next.js app — every command executed.

item.title: OpenAI's Dots demo had a 'slow morning' on stage — and the internet was brutal
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: At OpenAI's DevDay keynote, product lead Holly Li asked her Dots agent “Dottie” for an update — and got ten seconds of silence. Her joke that Dottie was having a “slow morning” became the event's most quoted line, and the clips went viral.

item.title: AWS open-sources Strands Decider 2B: a 2B model that never writes a word — and decides in 115 milliseconds
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AWS's Strands Labs released Strands Decider 2B on October 1, 2026: an open-source ~2B-parameter model that scores fixed options instead of generating text — a cheap, fast decision gate for AI agents.

item.title: Univer: give your AI agent a real spreadsheet — the open office harness, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Univer MCP (dream-num/univer-mcp, MIT) is a Model Context Protocol server that plugs AI agents straight into Univer, the 22K-star open-source office SDK. Wire it into Claude Code, point the agent at a live workbook, and have it build, format, and audit a real spreadsheet from a single prompt.

item.title: DaltonTx launches an AI antibody-discovery platform that folds 87,000 structures an hour — and logs every decision
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DaltonTx launched advanced antibody-discovery capabilities inside its Dalton platform: AI that designs, folds, and validates antibody candidates against real experimental data, with a chat interface that captures the reasoning behind every decision.

item.title: Robinhood puts AI agents inside its app: name a bot, fund a dedicated account, and let it trade for you
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At its HOOD Summit in Houston, Robinhood unveiled in-app AI trading agents that research markets and place trades on your behalf — approval on by default, but with a switch that hands the agent the keys. It is the closest thing yet to retail autopilot.

item.title: Turn any photo into an animatable 3D model: hands-on with img2threejs, the 17K-star image-to-code pipeline
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: img2threejs is an Apache-2.0 agent skill that rebuilds objects from a single photo as procedural Three.js code — quality-gated, staged, and self-correcting. We installed the skill, the img2 harness, ran its 1,364-test suite, and executed its intake gates for real. Every command verified.

item.title: Tencent rents 100,000 AI chips from Oracle for $7B — and the chips never enter China
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Tencent is reportedly leasing 100,000 advanced AI chips from Oracle's Southeast Asian data centers for about $7 billion over five years — hardware it cannot buy under US export rules, rented as compute it can.

item.title: Make Claude Code mod any PC game you own: a hands-on guide to universal-modder
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: universal-modder (rehan-remade/universal-modder) is the MIT toolkit that turns Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Gemini CLI into a game-modding agent: 12 engine playbooks, a fal-powered asset pipeline, the um CLI, and a knowledge base of field notes. Install the skills, scan your game library, brief the agent, and contribute your own field note.

item.title: Barclays goes all-in on Anthropic: Claude Code for half its developers by year-end, most engineers by 2027
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Barclays is expanding its strategic collaboration with Anthropic, putting Claude Code in the hands of half its developers by year-end and most software engineers in 2027 — while Claude systems already handle a million-plus knowledge searches and 120,000 client emails a day.

item.title: GRPO from scratch: implement the RL algorithm behind DeepSeek-R1 in ~200 lines of PyTorch
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Group Relative Policy Optimization — the RL algorithm behind DeepSeek-R1's reasoning — implemented from nothing in ~200 lines of PyTorch: sample groups of completions, score them with a verifiable reward, reinforce what beats the group average. No TRL, no critic, no value network — and every number measured on a real CPU run: 17% to 50% accuracy in about six minutes.

item.title: Ideogram 4.5 promises pixel-stable, drift-free multi-turn image editing
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Ideogram’s new 4.5 model takes aim at the slow drift that ruins multi-turn image edits — pixel shifts, color changes, texture artifacts — and pitches itself head-to-head against GPT Image 2.5 and Google’s Nano Banana.

item.title: Volantis raises $88M to break AI's memory wall with lasers: 220 memory chips per GPU
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: San Francisco startup Volantis raised $88 million to attack AI's most stubborn hardware bottleneck with laser light: VCSEL optical links could pack 220 memory chips around a single GPU, versus eight for Nvidia's best.

item.title: NPC-Forge: build conversational agents with zero ML — hands-on with the deterministic, CPU-only agent framework
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: NPC-Forge is a deterministic, CPU-only conversational-agent framework with no ML and no LLMs: a 24,000-intent terminal assistant, a built-in test suite, and an OpenAI-compatible gateway that serves every NPC as a model. Install it, test it, and build your own tool-calling NPC in one JSON file.

item.title: Boston Dynamics gave Atlas a new pair of hands — and Reddit is arguing about the missing pinky
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The new generation hand for Atlas has four fingers, 13 degrees of freedom, dense tactile sensors, and no pinky. The accompanying Boston Dynamics blog post explains exactly why — and the r/singularity thread that surfaced the video within hours went straight for the missing digit.

item.title: SoftBank wires the final $10B to OpenAI: Son's cumulative bet hits $64.6B for a 13% stake
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: SoftBank Group executed the third and final $10 billion tranche of its OpenAI follow-on investment on October 1, completing a $30 billion commitment unveiled in February. Son’s cumulative bet now stands at $64.6 billion for roughly 13% of the ChatGPT maker — funded by what Reuters calls the largest junk-bond sale in history.

item.title: XPENG takes the G9L global at the Paris Motor Show: its “AI flagship SUV” runs VLA 2.0 — and brings a robot lineup
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: XPENG announced today it will give its G9L — billed as a “Next-Gen AI Flagship SUV” running its VLA 2.0 model on the in-house Turing AI chip — its global launch at the 2026 Paris Motor Show on October 12, opening European order books alongside a “Physical AI” showcase of humanoid robots, flying cars, and live autonomous test rides with Tesla.

item.title: Hire an AI red team for the price of an API key: hands-on with Strix, the 65K-star autonomous pentesting agents
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Strix (usestrix/strix) sends autonomous AI agents to hack your app inside a Docker sandbox and reports only vulnerabilities they have proven with a working exploit. We installed 1.6.2, mapped every CLI flag, built a deliberately vulnerable target and proved its holes, and wired the CI gate — command by command.

item.title: ZoomInfo launches Agent Teams: AI agents that run the whole sales play — built on yesterday’s DoubleO.ai buy
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: ZoomInfo announced today Agent Teams, AI agents that run complete go-to-market plays from signal to action without human babysitting — built on the DoubleO.ai orchestration startup it acquired yesterday, available now in GTM Studio with no new SKU or contract.
